html:
The Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak is a beehive shaped brick tomb near Kazanlak in central Bulgaria, built around 300 BCE for a Thracian ruler and found by soldiers digging a shelter in 1944.

Its dome and corridor are covered with paintings: a funeral feast with the ruler and his wife holding hands, horses, a chariot race and battle scenes. They are among the best preserved Greek style paintings of their time. The Thracians, a people famed for horses, gold and the Orpheus legend, had kingdoms here in contact with the Greeks and Macedonia. The valley around Kazanlak holds many more Thracian tombs and is called the Valley of the Thracian Kings. The tomb has been a World Heritage Site since 1979; a copy is shown to visitors to protect the original.
